topic: Substantive Academic Editing vs. Surface Proofreading

copy.instagram:
We’ve all been there: staring at a draft at 2 AM, praying that fixing a few typos will magically bump your grade. Here’s the hard truth: grammar checkers won’t save a weak argument. 

Slide 1: The 2:2 Trap. You’re relying on software to fix errors while your actual points stay buried under repetitive, shaky logic. 

Slide 2: The 1st Class Blueprint. This is where the magic happens. We focus on substantive editing—rewriting clunky sentences, fixing your flow, and ensuring your argument actually answers the prompt. It’s not just about spelling; it’s about making your work sound like an expert wrote it. 

Stop submitting 'polished' drafts that still feel like a B-minus. Let’s get your work to the standard you’re actually capable of. 

Save this for your next deadline crunch. If you're stuck on a draft, hit the link in our bio to see how we can help you restructure. 

#universitylife #dissertationtips #essayhelp #studygram

Most students think proofreading is just fixing typos. That’s why so many get stuck at a 2:2. 

True academic editing is about rewriting for impact, logic, and register. If your argument is weak, no spellchecker will fix it. 

Want to know how to level up? Details in bio 👇

• Register Refinement: We swap informal language for precise, scholarly vocabulary. 
• Rubric Alignment: We make sure your work hits every single point your professor is looking for.
